title: Canary sculpting week plan + cross-team queue notes (Sep 2027)
content:
Overview:
This note captures a tight 7-day canary "sculpting" cadence for the upcoming release (feature bundle: routing optimizer + KV cache tweak + batching change). The goal: push gradual traffic, validate latencies, capture regression signals, and leave minimal blast radius. This is a working agenda — use it for on-call handoffs, queue ownership, and release notes drafts.

Quick context and risk:
- Routing optimizer changes can surface tail-latency regressions on long-seq requests.
- KV cache TTL change may increase cache misses for small prompts for first 30 minutes post-rollout.
- Batching tweak reduces peak GPU memory per-request but may change token throughput profiles.

Week plan (Sculpt sequence):
Day -3 (prep):
- Finalize smoke test set (see smoke-tests block). Owner: Marco.
- Lock quiet windows with infra and SRE. Quiet window: 02:00-06:00 UTC on Day 0.
- Create canary routing policy in staging. PR -> release-engineering/pull/512.

Day -2 (dry run):
- Dry-run traffic simulation on staging with production-like synthetic traces for 3h.
- Run resource soak: 4x sustained QPS for 2h.
- Verify telemetry: span tags, token counts, KV hit-rate metric exists.

Day -1 (preflight):
- Final go/no-go sync 30m. Meet: release-ops channel.
- Upload rollout config to release-configs S3.
- Notify support rotation and update playbook link.

Day 0 (canary start):
- 00:00 UTC: deploy canary image to region-a (10% of region capacity).
- 00:15 UTC: run full smoke test. If fail -> immediate rollback (see rollback matrix).
- 01:00 UTC: expand to 25% for region-a. Observe 90m.
- 03:30 UTC: if signals stable -> expand to 50% and enable throttling guardrails.
- 06:00 UTC: (end quiet window) hold, review telemetry summary, decide on region-wide expansion.

Day 1-3 (staggered expansion):
- Region-by-region expansion with 6h observation windows.
- Canary ticket owner rotates every 12h (morning/overnight).
- Rate-limit backoff thresholds: latency P99 increase >20% or error-rate >0.5% -> pause and inspect.

Daily cadence and queue notes (cross-team):
- Morning (09:00 UTC): quick triage summary posted to #release-ops with: observed latencies, errors, KV hit-rate, and overall token throughput.
- Midday (15:00 UTC): product & SRE sync if anomalies.
- Nightly (23:00 UTC): handoff doc to next on-call with explicit TODOs and pointer to current canary percentage.
- Queue ownership: assign two engineers from serving-runtime and one from observability as the primary responders. Secondary: infra-ops.

Quiet-window checklist (for Day 0):
- Confirm DB migrations (if any) are disabled.
- Rate-limiters in place; emergency throttle script tested.
- Pager thresholds verified for token queue depth and GPU OOM alarms.
- Support playbook updated with sample user-facing line.

Smoke-test catalogue (minimal set):
- smoke-01: single short prompt generation (<64 tokens) — assert latency < 120ms (p50), no errors.
- smoke-02: multi-turn chat (context 1k) — assert token continuity, no KV miss spike.
- smoke-03: long-seq decode (2–3k tokens) — assert tail latency within baseline + 30%.
- smoke-04: embedding endpoint sample — checksum vs golden.
- smoke-05: burst test 200QPS for 1 minute — check for queueing/backpressure.

Rollback matrix (fast decisions):
- Immediate rollback if: 1) crashlooping replicas > 1 for 10m; 2) P50 latency > 2x baseline for >15m; 3) error-rate > 2% sustained 5m.
- Partial rollback: scale canary down to 0% in region-X if P99 uptick > 30% and overall errors < 0.5% (indicates edge case).
- Post-rollback steps: create incident ticket, gather logs (traces + sample requests), tag release with "rolled-back".

Release notes (draft) — to be pasted into release email/notes:
- Summary: Shipping routing-optimizer v3.2, KV-cache TTL reduction, and batching window adjustment to improve throughput and reduce memory pressure on larger sequence workloads.
- User impact: expected improved throughput for small-to-medium prompts; short-duration cache miss increase after flip (should stabilize within 30m).
- Rollout plan: canary sculpting over 72 hours with per-region staged ramps; emergency rollback guardrails in place.
- Rollback guidance for customers: If you observe degraded latencies, contact support with a sample request id and indicate which region the calls originate from.
- Known limitations: long-sequence tail latency may show higher variance during first hour in some regions. We are instrumenting additional KV metrics for the follow-up patch.

Post-release checklist (first 48h):
- Collect token-level cost delta and per-model throughput. Owner: Lena.
- Run full regression eval set (batch job) and compare mean ROUGE/QA metrics.
- Lock the canary flag behind a config toggle for 7 days.
- If any regression detected, schedule hotfix branch and assign SLA meeting within 8 hours.

Notes to reviewers / TODOs:
- Marco: finalize the smoke test harness and add the new KV metrics to telemetry dashboard (dashboard id: conf:REL-KV-Panel).
- Jin: coordinate with customer-success to pre-brief the Top 20 customers on the small predicted latency blips.
- Aisha: prepare release email draft with the release notes block above and an abbreviated TL;DR for internal slack.

Observability pointers (links):
- Traces: /traces?service=inference&env=canary (placeholder)
- Dashboards: release-ops > canary-sculpting-2027-09
- Logs: central-elk -> query: "canary_id:2027-09-01"

If anything changes mid-run (unexpected OOMs, API schema changes, or external infra degradation), pause expansion and escalate to SRE lead (pager duty: srel+canary). Keep this doc as the single source for the week.

----- END working draft -----

(Informal notes recovered from meeting: "If we see KV miss rate jump only for requests >1200 tokens, suspect TTL boundary logic — iterate on TTL heuristics in next patch. Also consider temporary user-tier routing for heavy prompt customers to reduce impact.")
